subject: Weekly leadership handoff: priority handoff & QBR triage
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Leadership Distro <leadership@redwood.com>
Cc: olga.petrov@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Weekly leadership handoff: priority handoff & QBR triage

Team —

Quick handoff this morning ahead of the slice-of-day: below are the condensed wins / risks / asks for the week. I attached the working QBR draft (QBR-draft-v1.pdf). Please read the risks section — we need alignment on the mitigation runway by COB Monday so the GTM slides are locked.

Wins
- Hosted latency improvements live for the new batching kernel (observed 18% p50 reduction on synthetic load tests).
- Acme pilot completed security questionnaire (SOC2 evidence bundle sent).
- Dedicated pilot onboarding for Beta-3 customers on track (two customers migrated this week).

Top risks
1) Capacity squeeze for east-coast Dedicated clusters if we get Acme production go-live early Jan; projected 30% utilization spike. Owner: jonas_weber.
2) QBR narrative: we still have a slide gap on cost-per-inference attribution for quantized models — needs finance confirmation. Owner: markus_klein.
3) One outstanding redline in Acme contract (data residency clause) — legal asks Sanctioned language by Tuesday. External contact: Samir Rao.

Asks (short)
- Jonas: share an updated capacity plan (sheet attached) with conservative vs optimistic headroom by EOD Monday.
- Markus: confirm the finance metric (cost-per-token) and whether we can publish a conservative range for the QBR.
- Olga: lead the QBR narrative on Reliability + Degradation Plan (10m slot) — draft due Monday.

If you have objections to owners above, reply inline. I will consolidate into the QBR slide deck Monday morning.

Thanks,

Marissa
Marissa Cole | VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: QBR-draft-v1.pdf (PDF, 1.8MB)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, leadership@redwood.com
Cc: jonas.weber@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 11 Dec 2026 09:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Weekly leadership handoff: priority handoff & QBR triage

Thanks Marissa — good consolidation. A few clarifying points and updates from infra/serving:

- OKR check-in (week):
  * Serving runtime: on track for the December perf milestone (team validated kernel pass at 10k seq/s in staging). Small backlog on test harness automation (owned by markus_klein).
  * Reliability OKR: two P1s this week (both transient, no customer impact) — I'm logging follow-ups in the ops tracker.

- Risk triage notes:
  1) Capacity squeeze: Jonas, please add a conservative "peak concurrency +15%" scenario and an emergency spillover policy (region failover list + cost delta). If Dedicated can't absorb Acme in Jan, we need to offer a staged switchover (hosted fallback) in the mutual action plan.
  2) Cost-per-inference: Markus, if finance can't provide numbers, propose a placeholder range with an explicit footnote (methodology + sample workloads). We'll mark that slide as "under review" in the QBR.
  3) Acme redline: Laura, can you coordinate with Legal + Samir on the residency language? If Legal is comfortable with a regional-process clause, we can finalize.

- Logistics: I'm attaching the current OKR tracker export. I'll slot a 30m dry-run for the QBR next Wednesday 11:00-11:30 PT — can everyone please confirm availability by Monday EOD.

Action items assigned to owners are inline; I will produce a finalized action table after responses.

Olga
Olga Petrov | Head of Operations
Redwood Inference
Attachments: OKR-tracker-Dec11.csv (CSV, 34KB)

Adding the conservative scenario now — attached capacity-plan-v2.xlsx. Key callouts:
- Peak concurrency +15% scenario included with buffer lanes per region.
- Emergency spillover: primary failover to west-2 -> cost delta ~+22% token.
- Proposed short-term mitigation: enable Autoscale burst for Dedicated for Acme initial 2-week window (manual overspend guard).

I'll finalize numbers by Monday EOD after one more forecast run, but this should be good for the QBR talking points.

Jonas
Jonas Weber | Director, Platform Engineering
Redwood Inference

Looping in Samir to close the residency redline. Samir — thanks for the quick responses on the SOC2 artifacts; one outstanding ask from Legal is a narrowly scoped residency paragraph that confirms processing in the requested region with an operational fallback if required. Do you have language your legal team prefers? Happy to take a first pass and route to our counsel.

Separately: the Acme timeline still shows "production readiness by Jan 10". If that moves earlier, we need explicit signoff on both the support model (SRE on-call overlap) and SLA exceptions for a 30-day ramp. I'll include those as explicit bullets in the QBR risks slide unless I hear objections.

Laura
Laura Bennett | Chief Legal Officer
Redwood Inference

Thanks all — brief final consolidation so people have clear next steps before Monday: 

Action table (owners & due)
- Jonas Weber: capacity-plan-v2.xlsx — update with +15% conservative run and failover cost delta; due Mon COB.
- Markus Klein: finance cost range (or placeholder + methodology note) for cost-per-inference slide; due Mon COB.
- Laura Bennett: draft residency paragraph for Acme and confirm timeline signoff requirements; start intake with Samir today, due Tue EOD.
- Olga Petrov: QBR Reliability narrative draft & dry-run coordination (booked Wed 11:00 PT) — deliver draft Mon EOD.
- Marissa Cole: merge approved materials into QBR deck and share final draft on Drive; dry-run invite out to leadership.

Related links: QBR draft working folder (https://drive.redwood.com/drive/qbr/Acme-Q4-draft) — I will put the final slide deck there once consolidated.

If anything changes over the weekend flag the thread; otherwise I will collate Monday morning and lock the slide deck by 10:00am PT.

Marissa

Redwood Inference
